newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares jump 2.53 pct to new record.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares jump 2.53 pct to new record.

text.p: Istanbul shares leapt an average 2.53 percent amid selective buys on Thursday to resume the market's string of records after Wednesday's 1.29 percent downward correction, brokers said.

The IMKB-100 closed 2,320.38 points higher at 93,923.04, compared to Tuesday's previous all-time high closing of 92,797.71. Trade volume eased to 15.97 trillion lira ($154 million) from 16.17 trillion on Wednesday. ($156.3 million).
In dollar terms, the index stood at $0.9 from, compared to a record of $1 on April 8 and $0.67 at end-1995.
The index had gained 1.13 percent in the first two days of this week after last week's 5.49 percent surge and hit consequtive records in those seven days.

Brokers said the market pierced resistance at the index's 93,000 level and tested the 94,500, but weak volume caused activity to remain highly selective in light of end-1996 profit prospects of companies.
"Trade was quite lively and on the buying side today in contrast to yesterday. But this activity is not yet supported by an increase in volume," said Nazmi Sarikaya from Disbank.
